### Follow-up Questions

- Is this dish best treated as a warm salad or a hearty main, and how does roasting versus pan-frying the cauliflower change its texture and how it carries the chorizo fat?
- Which style of chorizo does the recipe assume — soft cooking chorizo (fresh, raw) or cured/semi-cured links — and how would that swap alter the cooking time and the amount of rendered paprika oil that flavors everything else?
- The recipe pairs canned green lentils for convenience; would Puy/du Puy or Pardina lentils cooked from dry meaningfully improve the dish, and is the trade-off in time worth it?
- Sherry vinegar appears as the only acid here — what is it balancing (the fat of the chorizo? the sweetness of roasted cauliflower?), and could it be pushed toward a fuller dressing?
- Why this specific spice pairing (cumin + coriander seed, crushed not ground) on cauliflower, and what does crushing rather than grinding actually contribute aromatically?

### Related Materials

- **Spanish Chorizo — origin, curing, and pimentón** (Wikipedia overview of varieties, fermentation, and the role of smoked paprika): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorizo
- **"The Story of Spanish Chorizo and How to Cook With It Today"** — practical guide to cooking vs. cured chorizo and rendering its fat: https://www.palenquemeat.com/post/the-story-of-spanish-chorizo-and-how-to-cook-with-it-today
- **"11 Types of Chorizo: How to Eat and Cook With Chorizo"** (MasterClass) — distinguishing Spanish cured, Spanish fresh, and Mexican chorizo so you pick the right one: https://www.masterclass.com/articles/how-to-eat-and-cook-with-chorizo
- **Fast chorizo, roasted cauliflower and almond salad** (Gourmet Traveller) — a very close cousin of this dish, useful as a method/ratio comparison: https://www.gourmettraveller.com.au/recipe/fast-recipes/chorizo-roasted-cauliflower-and-almond-salad-13662/
- **Chunky Roast Cauliflower & Chorizo** (Stonesoup) — minimalist take that highlights what's essential when you strip the dish back: https://thestonesoup.com/blog/2020/04/27/cauliflower-chorizo/
- **Yotam Ottolenghi's Roasted Cauliflower & Hazelnut Salad** (from *Jerusalem*, via Love & Lemons) — the template for cauliflower + nut + parsley + vinegar dressings this note clearly draws on: https://www.loveandlemons.com/roasted-cauliflower-hazelnut-salad-jerusalem/
- **"All about Spanish Chorizo"** (Benidorm Seriously) — background on *pimentón de la Vera* and why oak-smoked paprika defines the flavor: https://www.benidormseriously.com/all-about-spanish-chorizo
- **Cauliflower and French Lentils with Smoky Red Pepper Sauce** (The Curious Chickpea) — a vegetarian counterpoint showing how to get smokiness without the meat: https://www.thecuriouschickpea.com/cauliflower-french-lentils-smokey-red-pepper-sauce/

### Book & Podcast Recommendations

**Books**
- *Plenty More* by Yotam Ottolenghi — the spiritual home of spiced-roasted-cauliflower-with-nuts-and-sharp-dressing cooking that this recipe sits squarely within.
- *The Food Lab* by J. Kenji López-Alt — for the science of dry-roasting whole spices, rendering sausage fat, and why high-heat roasting transforms cauliflower.
- *Salt, Fat, Acid, Heat* by Samin Nosrat — a clean lens for understanding why chorizo (fat), sherry vinegar (acid), and roasting (heat) make this dish balance.

**Podcast episodes**
- *The Splendid Table* (host Francis Lam) — episodes on cooking with pulses/lentils, for getting texture and seasoning right with canned vs. dried.
- *Gastropod* (Cynthia Graber & Nicola Twilley), "The United States of Chiles" / paprika-and-peppers episodes — the New World pepper history behind pimentón and chorizo's color.
- *Milk Street Radio* (host Christopher Kimball) — recurring segments on smoked paprika and Spanish pantry staples that map directly onto this recipe's flavor base.
